Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NexCart Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NexCart Holdings' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; Morgan Chen, CTO; and Casey Lopez, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NexCart Holdings.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust marketplace momentum and sustained buyer engagement across our global platform. We saw significant growth in gross merchandise value, active buyer additions, and category penetration, reflecting the resilience of our hybrid first-party and third-party model in a maturing e-commerce environment where global penetration sits around 20-25% but is poised to hit 30% by 2027 according to eMarketer.

Our focus remains on scaling high-margin categories like beauty, apparel, and essentials while optimizing our supply chain for ultrafast delivery. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NexRecs AI recommendation engine, which we believe will significantly lift conversion rates through multimodal large language models that bundle products 25% more effectively than traditional systems.

We are investing heavily in GenAI applications for personalization, fraud detection, and dynamic pricing to counter aggressive pricing from players like Temu and TikTok Shop. We are focused on improving unit economics, with last-mile costs trending down through robotic automation in our fulfillment network.

We are expanding our presence in emerging markets like India and Brazil, where UPI payments and cross-border logistics integrations are driving outsized growth. Finally, we are committed to advancing sustainability through recycled packaging initiatives and green seller badges, enhancing loyalty among ESG-conscious cohorts.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $6.8 billion, an increase of 15% year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.7%, driven by a favorable shift toward private-label penetration now at 28% of GMV, which delivers around 52% margins compared to lower third-party averages, alongside COGS leverage from normalized inbound freight rates locked in at $3,500 per container through deals with Maersk and COSCO, yielding $180 million in supplier rebates. This builds on trends from a pandemic low of 34.2%, with six straight quarters of expansion thanks to AI-powered warehouse orchestration boosting throughput 35% and dynamic routing shifting volume to cheaper ground shipping, saving tens of millions. North America led at 40.1%, Europe at 37.2% despite VAT pressures, and emerging markets at 35.4% with nearshoring from Mexico cutting costs 15%. Operating expenses were $3.2 billion, representing 47% of revenue. Marketing spend rose modestly but delivered ROAS of 4.2x through refined Meta and Google targeting.

Diving deeper into gross margin trends, we've seen steady improvement from product mix favoring electronics and home goods partnerships akin to vendor-direct models, with AOV up 8% to $68 and returns stabilizing at 18% via computer vision for sorting. Fulfillment costs dipped as we deployed Symbotic-like robotics in 12 of 25 centers, handling 1.2 million units daily at 7.8% of revenue. Challenges like USPS rate hikes and Red Sea delays added minor pressure, but our diversified sourcing—45% North America, 35% APAC, 20% Europe—mitigates risks. We expect Q3 margins at 39.0-39.5% heading into year-end, scaling private labels to 32% and automating 80% of capacity.

Our net income for the quarter was $462 million, up 22% year-over-year from $379 million, well ahead of our guided $400-420 million range and consensus of around $410 million. This translated to diluted EPS of $1.05, a 24% increase from $0.85, beating Street expectations of $0.92 by 14%. Adjusted for a $18 million gain from divesting non-core European logistics, it was $444 million or $1.01 per share, still 19% above adjusted consensus. Top-line momentum from 18% GMV growth to $25.2 billion drove this, with take rates up 120 basis points to 28.5% on higher-value categories. Gross margins held at 42.1% despite carrier surcharges, bolstered by private-label 'NexEssentials' at 55% margins and robotic picking in top U.S. centers cutting fulfillment 80 basis points to 14.2%. Adjusted EBITDA hit $1.1 billion at 12.6% margins, up 200 basis points. North America contributed 60% at $278 million up 28%, Europe $112 million flat on FX, APAC $72 million up 15%. Headwinds like Red Sea delays added $45 million to COGS, but GenAI forecasting cut stockouts 25%, adding $0.08 to EPS. We're raising full-year net income to $1.85-1.95 billion, EPS $4.20-4.40 above consensus.

On GMV specifically, Q3 reached $25.2 billion, up 18% year-over-year and accelerating sequentially from prior quarters, surpassing our prior guide through active buyer strength and category gains. Marketplace GMV dominated at 65% share, with owned brands at 12% margins. This beat expectations amid holiday ramps, with North America at 75% of mix up 20-24%, Europe 12-15%, APAC/LATAM 25-30%.

Turning to active buyer growth, we added millions net new, pushing toward 180 million trailing-12-month actives, with retention at 75% up 300 basis points via NexCart Prime at 45 million members contributing 35% revenue. Acquisition CAC stabilized at $28, down from peaks, through paid social ROAS at 4.2x on shoppable videos and AR try-ons, organic SEO up 24%, and partnerships. Retention hit 72% for recent cohorts via AI recs lifting add-to-cart 19%, omnichannel PWAs, and Eco-Circle rewards. APAC led acquisition at 32%, North America retention at 76%.

We also updated our marketplace fee structure in March—referral fees up 150 basis points to 15.2%, FBN up 8-12% on labor costs, offset by rebates for 95% OTIF sellers and ACOS caps. Active sellers grew 4.2% to 2.8 million, pruning low-quality but boosting average GMV 11%. Sellers shifted to premium SKUs, electronics ASP up 14%, FBN dipped then rebounded to 65% with AI placement tools, ads at 23.1% ACOS. Take rate up 80 basis points, net seller margins improved to 15.8%. Regions varied: U.S. resilient, Europe sensitive, APAC adaptive. Tools like Fee Forecaster API cut churn 14%.

Seasonality played out as expected in this back-loaded business, with Q3 building toward Q4's 42-48% annual GMV share. Historical index: Q4 145, Q1 75, Q2 95, Q3 85. Minor Q2 deviation from macro compression in apparel and supply normalization was transitory, offset by AI personalization lifting repeats 15% and quick-commerce in APAC.

We ended the quarter with $4.2 billion in cash and equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance but raising on strength.

I'll now turn to forward guidance for Q4 and full FY2024, reflecting disciplined growth amid moderating spending offset by essentials strength and tech initiatives. Q4 GMV $28.0-29.0 billion, 18-22% YoY, up sequentially; full-year $105-108 billion, 16-19%. Drivers: 5 million net new buyers via tiered Prime perks like same-day over $35, AOV $85-87 on electronics bundles and ultrafast groceries in 50 metros, marketplace 65% mix with beauty +25%, apparel +18% via live-streaming. North America $21.0-21.8B +20-24%, Europe $4.2-4.4B +12-15%, APAC/LATAM $2.8B +25-30%. Q4 revenue $6.5-6.7B +12-15%, full-year $25.2-25.6B +13-15%, take rate 23.2-23.5%, fulfillment 16% growth, ads 20%+. Q4 adjusted EBITDA $1.20-1.30B at 18.4-19.4% margins, full-year $4.75-4.95B at 18.8-19.3%, via SG&A to 12.5%, last-mile $4.20 down 8%, FCF $3.8-4.0B funding buybacks and capex. $500M FY25 GenAI investment; risks tariffs, unemployment, but essentials 35% GMV and 85% repeats resilient. Path to 20%+ margins by FY26.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment scalability. Our shipping times improved by 25% with robotic sortation in 80% of 250+ centers and predictive AI reducing stockouts 40%. Fulfillment costs were down 8% year-over-year per unit. We are implementing micro-fulfillment for sub-15-minute grocery delivery in major metros, partnering with drone pilots like Wing.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from shoppable live-streaming events, hosting thousands with 25% AOV uplift, and sponsored products on video ads capturing Google share. Customer acquisition costs were $28. Our brand awareness increased by 24% via AR try-ons and influencer partnerships. We are focusing on high-LTV cohorts with GenAI email flows and Prime loyalty tiers.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Chen.

Morgan Chen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization via NexRecs and dynamic pricing engines using reinforcement learning. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 72% of orders. We're investing in GenAI for fraud detection, reducing chargebacks 15%, and SmartCart auto-upsells trained on billions of sessions.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Lopez.

Casey Lopez:
Thanks, Morgan. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 19% improvement in conversion rates because of our TensorFlow-based recs on Snowflake data lakes. We are also focusing on first-party data strategies for GDPR compliance and privacy-safe personalization.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you elaborate on Q3 GMV growth details, actuals versus guidance, YoY and QoQ, and key drivers by segment and region?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. As Jordan detailed, Q3 GMV hit $25.2 billion, smashing our prior range with 18% YoY and solid sequential acceleration from Q2's $12.8 billion scaled up on holiday momentum—wait, building on prior trends like Q2's 24% YoY to $12.8B beating $11.9-12.3B by 4%. Marketplace $10.2B subset up 27% YoY, first-party strong. Fashion +32%, beauty +28%, electronics resilient. North America 68% +22% YoY/9% QoQ via NexFast subs at 45M; Europe +35%/14%; APAC +42%/16% on India doubling. Active buyers 180M +16%, orders 188M +18%, AOV $68 +5% from SmartCart. Seller tools cut stockouts 30%, Green badges boosted attach. Guide Q3 was crushed; Q4 sets up 23-27% YoY.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. On net income and EPS, how did you outperform expectations, and what were the regional contributions and key margin levers?

Jordan Lee:
Emily, spot on—net income $462M +22% YoY ahead of $400-420M guide and consensus, EPS $1.05 +24% beating $0.92. Adjusted $1.01 still beat. Revenue $6.8B +15% on GMV $25.2B +18%, take rates +120bps to 28.5%. Gross 42.1% resilient despite surcharges via NexEssentials 55% margins, fulfillment -80bps to 14.2% on robotics. EBITDA $1.1B 12.6% +200bps. North America $278M 60% +28%, Europe $112M flat FX, APAC $72M +15%. Flywheel 2.0 GenAI added $0.08 EPS, omnichannel BOPIS +15% LTV. Raised FY net $1.85-1.95B, EPS $4.20-4.40.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
Thanks. Thoughts on seasonality—trends, Q2/Q3 deviations, and how you're mitigating for Q4?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, seasonality is pronounced: Q4 42-48% annual GMV historically, like FY23 $2.8B +28% BFCM AOV $145. Q1 trough 18-22%, Q2/Q3 20-25%. Q2 $1.1B flat 8% below norm from inflation compressing U.S. apparel -4% AOV, Europe -12% VAT/energy, offset APAC +22% Diwali. Promotional hangover, electronics mix down, logistics +2-3 days. But EBITDA 12.2% beat via 8.2x turns. Mitigants: AI recs +15% repeats, dynamic pricing +3% AOV, NovaPrime 18M +25% free returns -11% abandonment, marketplace to 22%. Q3 inline, Q4 +32% normalized.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays.

Lisa Wong:
Congrats team. Impact of fee structure changes on sellers—churn, mix shifts, adoption?

Riley Patel:
Thanks Lisa. March updates: referrals +150bps to 15.2%, FBN +8-12%/$0.45 inbound, rebates for OTIF>95%, ACOS caps. Sellers 2.8M +4.2% QoQ, 3.5% micro-churn but avg GMV +11% $450K. Premium pivot: electronics ASP +14% $185, fashion private-label +22%. FBN 62% dip to 65% rebound AI optimizer -28% stranding. Ads ACOS 23.1% +210bps, promos -9%. Take rate +80bps +$220M rev. Seller margins 15.8%. U.S. churn 2.1%, Europe 5.2%, APAC +12%. Fee API 92% accuracy -14% churn, dynamic pricing +7.2% conv. Q3 reaccel 6%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Bank of America.

David Patel:
Thanks. Active buyer growth details—acquisition CAC, retention by region, initiatives?

Morgan Chen:
David, actives 28.7M Q2 base scaling to 180M T12M +19% strongest since 2021. New 4.2M, churn <8% vs industry 12-15%. CAC $28 -11% YoY: Meta/TikTok 65% ROAS 4.2x AR videos +28% conv, Google 22%, SEO +24%, affiliates 1.1M zero CAC. APAC +32% livestreams, U.S. +14% ZIP retarget, Europe +12% first-party data. Retention 72% +300bps, 90-day repeats 41%, Prime 9.2M 2.5x LTV $450. AI recs +19% ATC TensorFlow/Snowflake bundles +14% AOV, PWAs 68% app ret, Eco-Circle +18% GenZ. NA 76%, APAC 69%. FY target 20-22%, GenAI emails, grocery pilots.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Citi.

Rachel Kim:
Solid results. Forward guidance details on revenue, GMV, profitability—drivers, risks?

Casey Lopez:
Rachel, Q4 GMV $28-29B 18-22% YoY >Q3 $25.2B, FY $105-108B 16-19%. Buyers +5M loyalty tiers same-day >$35, AOV $85-87 electronics/groceries, mix beauty +25% apparel +18% live. NA $21-21.8B +20-24% drone, Europe $4.2-4.4B +12-15% 10M subs, APAC/LATAM $2.8B +25-30% UPI/Mercado. Rev Q4 $6.5-6.7B +12-15% take 23.2-23.5%, FY $25.2-25.6B +13-15%, ads +20%. EBITDA Q4 $1.20-1.30B 18.4-19.4% +150-250bps, FY $4.75-4.95B 18.8-19.3% +200bps: SG&A 12.5% ZBB -$150M, last-mile $4.20 -8% robotics, FCF $3.8-4.0B buybacks/capex 6%. $500M FY25 GenAI vs Temu. Risks tariffs 10-15% GMV/UE>4.2%, but essentials 35%/85% repeats. 20%+ margins FY26.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
